sections.title: An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents
sections.abstract: A controlled study varies planning, action space, and context management across 176 settings and four models on SWE-Bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.1.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors isolate how context management, planning, and action-space design affect accuracy, trajectory length, and cost.
sections.caveat: Evidence is limited to the evaluated models, benchmarks, and harness components.

sections.title: Not All AI Agents Are Equal: Characterizing Resource and Performance Dynamics
sections.abstract: Measurements across retrieval, web-search, and coding agents reveal task-dependent CPU, disk-I/O, and memory bottlenecks and motivate resource-aware scheduling.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose CPU-aware tool admission and task-aware CPU allocation.
sections.caveat: Gains are reported for the paper's workloads and deployment configuration.

sections.title: RAFT: A Stateful Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Troubleshooting Agents
sections.abstract: RAFT represents historical support cases as stateful chains, retrieves matching intermediate states, and returns the parent-case trajectory for troubleshooting.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce entry-level retrieval over directed case timelines, with an optional graph linking similar cases.
sections.caveat: The main benchmark is synthetic and the real Jira evaluation is directional evidence.

sections.title: Perception, Layout, and Validation: Calibrated Confidence for Reliable Straight-Through Processing of Financial Documents
sections.abstract: A decomposed confidence score plus conformal risk control improves the reliability and usable coverage of automated financial-document extraction.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine perception, layout, and validation signals with conformal risk control.
sections.caveat: Coverage and error results are empirical on selected datasets and models.

sections.title: Can Data Attribution Filter Out Subliminal Learning? Not Reliably
sections.abstract: An evaluation of three gradient-based data-attribution methods finds partial, inconsistent mitigation of subliminal learning across models and settings.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors show EK-FAC can mitigate a significant part of the effect in some settings, while other methods often fall short.

sections.title: Refuse, Decompose, Refresh: A Claim-Safe Protocol for Closed-Loop AI Evaluation
sections.abstract: A protocol for closed-loop evaluation separates unsupported claims, operational false admission, and distribution-shift alarms.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors connect observable support, statistical calibration, and justified claims in an evaluation contract.
sections.caveat: Results come from an aggregate-only simulator.

sections.title: Tailored to you: longitudinal effects of personalising language models
sections.abstract: A five-day, 992-participant study compares baseline, memory-based, and survey-based personalization.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report distinct effects of personalization on disclosure, perceived creepiness, and regret.

sections.title: Language-model groups overstate consensus when replaying human deliberation on a reasoning task
sections.abstract: Replaying 100 human Wason groups with matched LLM groups shows simulated groups are more consensual and consensus does not reliably track collective accuracy.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper provides a scoring-explicit test of whether belief-anchored LLM groups can estimate human deliberative outcomes.
sections.caveat: The task is a Wason reasoning setting.
